blind_solver_concerns.concern: I assumed the oil column connects the two piston faces, so the small piston sits lower by h and the force includes a rho*g*h term. I took the pistons as light and the atmosphere as cancelling on both outer faces.

The problem doesn't say whether the manometer height difference is measured with the flowing liquid filling the tubing above the mercury. I assumed it is, so dp=(rho_m-rho)*g*h. The pipe is horizontal, so there is no elevation term.
Compression assumed reversible (quasi-static) adiabatic for an ideal gas.
Heat given up by the original warm water taken as m_w c (T0 - Tf); the ice fully melts as stated, and I checked that it does.
Emissivity assumed equal; scaling P ~ R^2 T^4 used.
Specific heat given as 4180 here versus 4186 in the sibling items; used as stated.
No phase change or boiling assumed; the water stays below 373 K.
Height taken as vertical oil-column difference between piston faces, pistons massless; otherwise no ambiguity. Other items had no concerns.
Conversion of u to energy or kg is not given; used 1 u = 931.494 MeV/c^2. Recoil taken non-relativistically with the full Bohr transition energy as the photon energy.
Conversion of u to kg is not given; used 1.66054e-27 kg.
Uncertainty-principle estimate only, not an exact result for Z other than 1.

The magnetic field is vertical on an inclined rail, so the emf is B L v cos(theta) and the force along the incline is B I L cos(theta). The terminal speed therefore has a cos^2(theta) in the denominator. I assumed the rod stays horizontal and the rails are the only incline. Other items had no ambiguity.
Non-relativistic well energies assumed; the rest energy is only used via mc^2 in E_n. No other ambiguity in q001-q004.
